algorithm_name: Safe Neural Horizon PWM with Event-Triggered Twin Feedback
algorithm_identity_tuple: protected AI-PWM Safety Gateway with no raw low-side gate access

not_allowed: full no-feedback operation under unknown load and drift

legal_vector_horizon_search.why_it_matters: SNH-PWM optimizes finite sequences of legal inverter vectors instead of a continuous voltage reference.

neural_cost_shaping.why_it_matters: The neural layer shapes the MPC-like cost, rather than replacing only a PI loop.

event_triggered_twin_feedback.why_it_matters: The control loop explicitly trades feedback usage against model uncertainty and residuals.

protected_ai_pwm_gateway.why_it_matters: The AI can request only legal vector IDs; raw high/low gate access remains outside the AI interface.

multiobjective_drive_cost.why_it_matters: The objective jointly covers tracking, current stress, switching/loss/thermal/ripple, feedback economy, and risk.

deadbeat_current_baseline.snh_distinction: Deadbeat control targets one-step current matching; SNH-PWM optimizes a broader multiobjective drive cost.

dtc_hysteresis_baseline.snh_distinction: DTC hysteresis follows torque/flux comparator commands; SNH-PWM optimizes predicted vector sequences under risk and feedback costs.

dtc_svm_baseline.snh_distinction: DTC-SVM synthesizes a torque/flux voltage reference; SNH-PWM optimizes legal vector sequences directly.

fcs_mpc_one_step_baseline.snh_distinction: One-step FCS-MPC predicts legal vectors for one tick; SNH-PWM adds horizon search, neural shaping, and event feedback.

foc_svm_key_baseline.snh_distinction: FOC-SVM synthesizes dq voltage references and then selects an SVM-like vector; SNH-PWM searches vector sequences directly.

missing_snh_features: explicit horizon-search novelty over the prior H1 architecture
protected_ai_pwm_h1_baseline.snh_distinction: SNH-PWM generalizes the prior protected one-step AI-PWM into a horizon controller with event/twin/risk costs.

sensorless_adaptive_foc_baseline.snh_distinction: Sensorless/adaptive FOC estimates speed/Rs for classical FOC; SNH-PWM uses twin uncertainty inside vector-sequence selection.

warnings: This proves a distinct host-simulated control-law identity, not MCU/HIL/bench readiness or universal superiority.
